title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: Three different pairs of shoes are placed in a row so that no left shoe is next to a right shoe from a different pair. In how many ways can these six shoes be lined up?

solutions.text: Wherever an \(L\) meets an \(R\) in the side pattern, those two shoes must be mates. Thus an interior run cannot have length \(1:\) its lone shoe would have to be the mate of both neighbors. With three \(L\)’s and three \(R\)’s, the only possible patterns are \(LLLRRR,\) \(RRRLLL,\) \(LLRRRL,\) \(LRRLLR,\) \(LRRRLL,\) \(RLLLRR,\) \(RLLRRL,\) and \(RRLLLR.\) For either one-switch pattern, choose the pair at the switch and order the remaining shoes, giving \(3\cdot2\cdot2=12\) arrangements. Each of the other six patterns has \(6\) assignments of the three pairs to its switches. Hence the total is \(2\cdot12+6\cdot6=60.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: The rule says: wherever a left shoe touches a right shoe, they must be mates from the same pair
Case on the left/right pattern of the six spots; each place where the side switches pins down one pair
